title: Shorter sliding windows again: short_window = seq//8 (512 -> 256)
description: One line in GPT._compute_window_sizes: short_window = long_window // 4 -> // 8 (512 -> 256), WINDOW_PATTERN still SSSL; nothing else touched.
reflection: val_bpb 0.988725 at 490.2M tokens, 1870 steps, MFU 34.61%, 45.0GB, queued_s 327, FLOPs/token 2.108e8. Control is my own r02 pair at //4 (0.989668/0.989981, mean 0.989825, 486.4M tokens), one line apart: raw delta -0.0011, about 1.5 sd on the per-contrast SE, and the lowest number in the cell. Correcting for the +3.8M tokens at the within-cluster slope (-0.00013/1M) leaves a quality residual of about -0.0006 -- same sign as the 1024->512 cut but a third of the size, so the window axis is decaying fast. Two corrections to my own proposal: (1) my FLOP arithmetic was wrong, the cut is -4.3% (220.4 -> 210.8M/token), not -8.7% -- I mis-split the SSSL pattern; (2) the kernel tax is now nearly total: -4.3% arithmetic bought only +0.8% tokens because FA3 MFU fell 35.86 -> 34.61. At window 128 the MFU loss would very likely exceed the FLOP saving outright, so this axis should be considered closed at 256 on throughput grounds regardless of quality. Note my FLOPs/token is now identical to a0's 'SSSS' (7 short at 512 + 1 long), so those two runs are a clean equal-compute test of where to spend the span: many medium windows vs few narrow ones plus globals.
